Beginner Chest Workout at Home

A beginner-friendly dumbbell chest routine designed to target all areas of the pectoral muscles from home. Focus on controlled movements, proper form, and muscle contraction.

15–20 min
Duration
5
Exercises
1 Circuit
Blocks
Beginner Dumbbells Yoga Mat
0 of 5 done

Exercise Flow

Check off each exercise as you complete sets. Rest timer at the bottom.
01

Kneeling Alternating Dumbbell Front Raises

3 × 20 reps
Upper ChestAnterior Deltoids
  • Keep core engaged while kneeling tall
  • Raise dumbbells sequentially across the upper chest with control

Why: Targets the clavicular head (upper portion) of the chest along with the front shoulders.

02

Kneeling Dumbbell Overhead Raises

3 × 20 reps
Lower ChestUpper ChestShoulders
  • Lift both dumbbells simultaneously overhead smoothly
  • Maintain a neutral spine and avoid arching the lower back

Why: Engages chest fibers through an extended range of motion.

03

Dumbbell Floor Press

3 × 20 reps
Pectoralis MajorTriceps
  • Lie flat on the floor with knees bent and feet flat
  • Press dumbbells upward until arms are fully extended without locking elbows

Why: Builds mid-chest strength and upper body pressing power safely on the floor.

04

Dumbbell Floor Flyes

3 × 20 reps
Inner ChestOuter Chest
  • Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
  • Lower dumbbells wide until upper arms lightly touch the floor, then squeeze chest at top

Why: Isolates the pectoral muscles and improves chest expansion and contraction.

05

Floor Dumbbell Pullover

3 × 20 reps
Upper ChestLatsSerratus Anterior
  • Hold a single dumbbell with both hands extended over chest
  • Lower dumbbell overhead toward the floor keeping core tight and control the descent

Why: Expands the rib cage and isolates the upper chest and serratus muscles.

Trainer Tips

  • Focus on peak contraction at the top of every repetition rather than rushing.
  • Choose a light to moderate dumbbell weight to maintain strict form and reduce shoulder strain.
